title: Canadian Light Source
content:
The Canadian Light Source (CLS) is Canada's national synchrotron light source, a third-generation 2.9 GeV facility at the University of Saskatchewan in Saskatoon that opened in 2004. Operated by Canadian Light Source Inc., it serves over 1,000 academic, government and industry researchers annually across beamlines offering X-ray spectroscopy, diffraction and imaging from the macro to the nanoscale.

These tools support advanced materials research, including non-destructive study of pore structure and chemistry in porous and nanostructured materials such as aerogels. A dedicated Industry Services group provides fee-for-service access, from purchased beamtime to full-service experimental design, execution and analysis, letting companies access world-class characterization without owning the instruments.
excerpt: Canada's national synchrotron in Saskatoon, offering spectroscopy, diffraction and imaging beamlines plus fee-for-service industry characterization.
